cap: Feminizing therapy, puberty blockers and masculinizing therapy compared row by row. Each drug's mechanism predicts its expected changes, its main risk and the laboratory test that monitors it: potassium for spironolactone, bone density for a blocker, and hematocrit for testosterone. Neither hormone regimen is contraception.
teach: Read down a column to learn one regimen, then across the risk and monitoring rows to see why each test is chosen. Spironolactone blocks aldosterone as well as androgen receptors, so potassium rises. Oral estrogen passes through the liver first and raises clotting factors, so transdermal estradiol carries less VTE risk. Testosterone stimulates erythropoietin, so hematocrit climbs. A continuous GnRH agonist lowers sex steroids during the years of peak bone accrual, so bone density is followed.
